subject: Capacity orchestration: APAC pilot + EU failover lanes (pricing & timelines)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Melissa Torres <melissa.torres@edgecraft.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity orchestration: APAC pilot + EU failover lanes (pricing & timelines)

Team / Melissa —

Quick summary: EdgeCraft is ready to run a 3-month APAC pilot (Singapore) tied to an upcoming product launch. They asked for an initial committed footprint we can reserve and guarantee, plus an EU failover lane for GDPR-sensitive traffic. They want: predictable latency (~<120ms p95 to SG), predictable monthly unit cost for billing, and a quick onramp (2–3 week lead time).

Ask: Can infra and sales ops confirm a concrete sizing recommendation and a ballpark cost table we can present to EdgeCraft by EOD Monday? I sketched a model attached (edgecraft_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) with two scenarios: "pilot-min" (4 A100-equivalent nodes reserved, burst pool available) and "pilot-scale" (12 nodes reserved, staged rollout).

Key constraints to assume:
- Pilot duration: 3 months (option to extend)
- Traffic shape: daily peak windows (see attached sample), token profile heavy on short chat (1–2k tokens/session)
- Failover lane in EU: warm standby (hot-warm) with cross-region KV cache fallback

Melissa — if you can confirm expected QPS and major peak hours that helps refine the sizing.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: sizing + cost delta (reserved vs burst) for SG + Dublin failover
- Soojin: SLO impact and recommended pre-warm strategy (KV cache sizing, prefix caching)
- Irene: lead time / provisioning checklist (infra ticket and playbook)

Attachments: edgecraft_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | seAN.gallagher@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Melissa Torres <melissa.torres@edgecraft.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity orchestration: APAC pilot + EU failover lanes (pricing & timelines)

Sean — good framing. I reviewed the model and sketched two practical options and a quick cost estimate (attached). High level:

Option A — Reserved pilot (predictable, higher committed cost):
- Start: 4 A100-equivalent instances (we map to 1x reserved unit = 8 A100-ish GPUs on our pool; using smaller quantized instances for SG to reduce cost).
- Scale path: 4 -> 8 in week 3 if 7-day rolling average load exceeds 70% utilization.
- EU failover: 2 warm nodes in Dublin (standby, <50% warm utilization), cross-region failover route.
- Pros: tight latency control, predictable billing.
- Cons: higher committed TCO if not used.

Option B — Hybrid burst (lower commitment, more orchestration):
- Start: 2 reserved nodes + burst buffer (deal-linked surge lane) of up to additional 10 nodes in SG during peak windows.
- EU failover: fully-burstable lane with cold-warm pre-warm cadence (pre-warm 1–2 nodes 30min before expected peaks).
- Pros: lower baseline cost, faster elasticity.
- Cons: slightly higher p95 variability during cold starts; more ops complexity.

Attached: cost_estimate_apac_eu.pdf — rough monthly delta (reserved vs hybrid) including network, cross-region egress assumptions. I assumed the traffic Melissa flagged in the model: 2–3M tokens/day with concentrated peaks.

Operational notes:
- If EdgeCraft needs firm SLA credits, we should push for Option A with a 3-month commitment and an explicit surge budget.
- For sizing accuracy, we need their hourly expected QPS for the first 6 weeks (Melissa, if you can share CSV that’s ideal).

I can finalize a one-page pricing table for the customer-facing proposal if you want to present both options.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: cost_estimate_apac_eu.pdf (PDF)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Melissa Torres <melissa.torres@edgecraft.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity orchestration: APAC pilot + EU failover lanes (pricing & timelines)

Thanks — quick follow-ups on SLO/ops implications:

- Latency target: <120ms p95 to SG is achievable with reserved units and local cache. With burst model expect occasional ~200–300ms spikes during cold scale (depends on prefix cache hit rate).
- Cache sizing: for chat-heavy workloads, allocate ~40GB KV cache per 4-node block; prefix caching saves ~30% token cost if customer traffic has conversational locality.
- Warm-up pattern: recommend automated pre-warm triggers (webhook from EdgeCraft or scheduled pre-warm based on their release calendar). Pre-warm 2 nodes 30–45 minutes pre-peak.
- Monitoring: add a short eval prompt set (5–10 prompts) to validate generation quality post-failover; tie alerts to rate of rollback attempts.

If we go hybrid, we should also include a 24/7 escalation pact for the first 4 weeks. I'll draft the SLO addendum language.

Soojin
Infra Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Melissa Torres <melissa.torres@edgecraft.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 02:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity orchestration: APAC pilot + EU failover lanes (pricing & timelines)

Appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifications from our side: we expect regional peaks aligned with APAC business hours (~2200–0200 UTC) with predicted peak QPS ~120 rps and average session 1.5k tokens. Attached is our weekly sample (edgecraft_traffic_weekly.csv) — it's a short extract.

Our priorities: predictable cost for the pilot (we'll be convincing procurement) and a simple failover behavior (traffic should not land in US). We prefer reserved for SG if the delta vs hybrid is <20% — procurement hates complexity. But we also need a clear playbook for rollback if generation quality regressions happen after failover.

We can sign a 3-month pilot SOW quickly if you provide:
- A short onramp timeline (exact days to provision)
- A one-page pricing matrix (reserved vs hybrid)
- Failover playbook and SLO language we can include in our SOW

Melissa
Head of Platform, EdgeCraft AI
Attachments: edgecraft_traffic_weekly.csv (CSV sample)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Melissa Torres <melissa.torres@edgecraft.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity orchestration: APAC pilot + EU failover lanes (pricing & timelines)

Thanks, Melissa — that's exactly the data we needed. Action summary and owners: 

1) Karthik: produce a one-page pricing matrix (reserved vs hybrid) with the two concrete SKUs (4-node reserved start / 2-reserved+burst). Deliverable: PDF for procurement by EOD Wed (2025-09-17). Reference: cost_estimate_apac_eu.pdf.
2) Soojin: draft a two-paragraph SLO/failover playbook and a 4-week escalation window; include cache sizing. Deliverable: draft by Tue noon.
3) Irene: open infra ticket INFRA-4821 (I created the stub) and list exact time-to-provision and checklist for SG nodes + Dublin warm standby. Please include estimated calendar days per step.
4) Melissa: we'll aim for 2–3 week provision timeline if we have committed units — we'll confirm once Karthik and Irene finalize numbers.

I'll assemble these into a one-page SOW and the HubSpot deal record (linked). If everyone is aligned, I'll send the SOW and draft SLR language to procurement.

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
